content.text: Found the main causes; checking your actual artifact in the database to confirm.

Short version: the artifact can't see recurring at all, and the after-sync analysis does run on its own, but most of what it finds stays on the Agents page instead of showing on Home.

## 1. Why the artifact shows zero recurring
Artifacts can only read these data sources: transactions, investigate, cashflow, balances, accounts and goals (`lib/ai/artifact-data.ts:15`). None of them is recurring. So when your "Subscription radar" was built, it tried to work recurring out by itself: it took the last 50 transactions and counted transactions per merchant. It never read your confirmed recurring schedules, so it finds nothing.

A second problem: the saved queries have fixed dates (`to: "2026-10-27"`), so the artifact won't move forward as new days come in.

**Fix:** add a `recurring` source that returns your confirmed schedules, the same list the Recurring page shows, and make the builder use relative periods like "last 6 months" instead of fixed dates.

## 2. What happens after a sync
After each sync that brings in new rows, an agent team runs by itself (`workflows/import-file.ts:30`):

| Agent | What it does now |
|---|---|
| Categorizer | **Applies its picks by itself**, with Undo (130 applied this week) |
| Recurring detective | Only suggests (20 waiting) |
| Anomaly hunter | Only suggests (61 waiting) |
| Budget, forecaster, writer | Only suggest |

You don't need to run a deep analysis by hand. The catch is that all of these suggestions sit on `/ai/agents`. Home only shows IOUs, expenses, balances and recurring cards.

## 3. Gaps I found against what you want
- **Uncategorized rows never reach Home.** You have **344 posted transactions with no category**. Whatever the categorizer can't place, or isn't sure about, just stays there.
- **Recurring is detected twice.** The agent team saves its own recurring suggestions (20) on the Agents page. Home runs a separate check that makes its own cards (21). You end up seeing the same thing in two places.
- **"Not recurring" is mostly respected already.** Home won't show a card again once you dismiss it, and a series marked "not recurring" is skipped in both places. One exception: if you dismiss a suggestion on the Agents page instead of Home, Home can still raise it.
- **Some categorizer results are stuck:** 2 are frozen at "applying" and 5 failed.

## What I'd do
1. Add a `recurring` source to artifacts and switch them to relative date ranges.
2. Put one "N uncategorized transactions" card on Home next to IOUs. It links to the Organization page, and the count goes down as you categorize.
3. Have one place make recurring suggestions: Home's cards. The agent team would stop saving its own. Then a single "Not recurring" covers everything.
4. Show anomalies on Home as one summary card (for example "3 possible duplicates, 1 price increase") rather than 61 separate cards.

One question decides how I build 2 and 4: when something lands on Home, do you want **one card per item** or **one summary card per type** that links to a list? I'd go with summary cards. 344 separate uncategorized cards would bury your IOUs.

content.text:
#1 is done and committed as `56061922` and `a77095db` on branch `t3/sync-analysis-recurring`; I haven't pushed. Artifacts can now read your confirmed recurring payments, and their saved dates move forward each day. The full test suite, lint and type check pass, but I didn't open an artifact in the running app.

Your current "Subscription radar" won't change by itself, because its saved queries were written before the recurring source existed. Ask the AI to rebuild it once and it will pick up your recurring payments.

## 2–4: how it will look

**The idea:** after each sync the app checks everything by itself. It applies what it's confident about, and Home shows what's left for you to decide, one card per type. The Agents page is where you can see what happened and why.

### Home, in simple words
Your normal overview, plus a **"Waiting for you"** strip:

- **IOU, expense and balance cards**: same as now, one card each.
- **"344 transactions need a category"**: one card with a **Sort them** button.
- **"5 payments look recurring"**: one card with a **Review** button.
- **"3 things look off"** (a possible duplicate, a price increase, an unusual charge): one card with a **Review** button.

A summary card disappears once its count reaches 0. Things the app already handled (auto-categorized rows) don't show here; there's just a small line like "Sorted 130 transactions automatically · Undo".

### Agents page, in simple words
This becomes the **history of what the app did by itself**, not a second inbox:
- One entry per sync: "Synced Oct 30 · categorized 42 · found 2 recurring · 1 possible duplicate".
- Open an entry to see the evidence for each finding and an Undo for anything applied automatically.
- No separate Accept/Reject buttons here anymore. Decisions all happen from Home, so dismissing something in one place can't leave it showing in the other.

### How you choose from a summary card
Tapping **Review** opens a sheet on top of Home with that type's items listed, each with one-tap answers:

| Card | Each row shows | Your choices |
|---|---|---|
| Recurring | "Netflix · €12.99 monthly · 6 times" | **Yes, recurring** / **Not recurring** |
| Uncategorized | grouped by merchant: "REWE · 23 transactions" | pick a category (it suggests one), or **Skip** |
| Looks off | "Possible duplicate: Amazon €34.99 twice on Oct 12" | **It's fine** / **Fix it** (open the transaction) |

- Uncategorized rows are grouped by merchant, so 344 rows become maybe 30 choices. Picking a category for a group also saves a rule, so the next sync categorizes that merchant by itself.
- "Not recurring" and "It's fine" are remembered, so those items never come back.
- Each sheet has a **Do all suggested** button for when the suggestions look right.

Should I build it this way? It would be about four commits: Home summary cards, the review sheet, making Home the only source of recurring suggestions, and turning the Agents page into history.
Yes and once done merge to main
